title: Coefficient adjunction stages before refinement
statement: Under exactly the geometric and coefficient hypotheses of def-sf-constructible-exceptional-coefficient-construction-data there exist R : CoefficientConstructionRing, F : CoefficientConstructionFields R, and M : CoefficientConstructionCommon R F, satisfying CoefficientConstructionNormalization, including its common-stage transition clause: the closed left functor is defined on pair-category arrows through the common-stage transitions and the rational scalar q. These supply the operations at every compactification and coefficient stage, normalized scalar mates, and ring scalar unitors and associators. No comparison between different compactifications is asserted. This is steps 1 through 5 of the existing construction proof.

source.place: Coefficient adjunction stages before refinement; normalized coefficient construction in the existing assembly node.

proof.text: Obtain the finite/integral ring-only assembly A, with its common endpoint scalar choices and shift-compatible ambient left realizations.
Extend A by rational/closed operations, rational-left realizations and field/common comparisons using field-stage completion.

Construct R by RingStageAssembly.complete: use the given ring operations at finite and integral stages and the new operations at rational/closed stages; retain all ring scalars, counit mates and their normalizations verbatim. The leftShift field follows by cases on RingStage from A.leftShift.

Use the five supplied field normalization families for localization shifts, localization identity and common shifts. For commonTransitionNatural, specialize M.common_morphism_normalized at the identity arrow on the scalar extension of K. Functoriality removes its map of identity and its composite with identity. Left-compose by the stage-i q; reassociation and q.hom q.inv = identity cancel the inverse q. This is precisely the common-stage transition equation. No new existence or normalization assumption is made.

proof_origin.place: Finite/integral versus field-stage decomposition of existing steps 1--5; final common-transition equation is the identity-arrow specialization of the existing representativeAction field.
